claims.claim: **In healthy children, influenza usually settles by itself**, but severe disease occurs both in previously well children and in those with risk factors.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Influenza' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Influenza/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Incubation 1–4 days (average 2).** Infectious from 24 hours before symptoms for 4–7 days of illness — longer in young or immunodeficient children. PCR can stay positive for up to 3 weeks.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Influenza' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Influenza/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Younger children** are less likely to have respiratory features and more likely to have febrile seizures, gastrointestinal features and severe disease.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Influenza' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Influenza/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Severe features — consider treatment:** pneumonia · secondary bacterial infection (especially *S. aureus*, *S. pneumoniae*) · respiratory failure · neurological complications (cerebellar ataxia, aseptic meningitis, encephalopathy/encephalitis, Guillain-Barré) · rhabdomyolysis · myocarditis/pericarditis · Reye syndrome (aspirin).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Influenza' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Influenza/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Risk factors — consider treatment:** severe chronic disease (neurological, respiratory, cardiac, haematological including sickle cell, hepatic, CKD, diabetes, obesity over 95th centile) · genetic syndromes such as trisomy 21 · neuromuscular disease · prematurity under 37/40 · immunosuppression · pregnancy · long-term aspirin.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Influenza' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Influenza/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **A positive influenza PCR in an unwell child does not rule out a serious bacterial infection, whether co-existing or secondary.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Influenza' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Influenza/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Immunisation status does not change management** of suspected influenza.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Influenza' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Influenza/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Mild flu-like illness needs no test.** Test when the result will change management — e.g. cohorting inpatients, or directing therapy in high-risk children.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Influenza' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Influenza/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Supportive care** (hydration, analgesia, respiratory support); **isolate or cohort admitted children.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Influenza' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Influenza/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Hospitalised children with risk factors or severe features: start oseltamivir empirically.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Influenza' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Influenza/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Oseltamivir is usually first line, oral or nasogastric.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Influenza' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Influenza/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Benefit is modest** — about 1 day shorter illness on average, and it may prevent severe disease. **Most effective started within 48 hours**; some benefit up to 7 days. Neuraminidase inhibitors do nothing for other viruses.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Influenza' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Influenza/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Oseltamivir comes as 30, 45 or 75 mg capsules or a 6 mg/mL suspension**; capsule contents can be dissolved in water for immediate use.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Influenza' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Influenza/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Side effects:** headache; nausea and vomiting — give with food; vomiting is twice as likely (4–8% of unwell children). **Seek advice in renal impairment.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Influenza' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Influenza/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Oseltamivir treatment, oral bd for 5 days — preterm and infants:** PMA under 38 weeks: 1 mg/kg per dose · PMA 38–40 weeks: 1.5 mg/kg per dose · term birth to 12 months: 3 mg/kg per dose.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Influenza' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Influenza/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Oseltamivir treatment, 1–18 years, oral bd for 5 days:** under 15 kg 30 mg · 15–23 kg 45 mg · 23–40 kg 60 mg · over 40 kg 75 mg.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Influenza' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Influenza/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Peramivir (IV):** specialist advice, inpatients only, over 2 years, when the enteral route is not appropriate.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Influenza' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Influenza/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **After significant exposure** (within 1 metre for over 15 minutes without PPE), **give oseltamivir prophylaxis** to children and family members who have personal risk factors, household contacts with risk factors, household contacts aged 65 or over, or pregnant or up to 2 weeks post-partum.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Influenza' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Influenza/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Oseltamivir prophylaxis, oral once daily for 10 days:** term birth to 12 months 3 mg/kg/dose; 1–18 years under 15 kg 30 mg · 15–23 kg 45 mg · 23–40 kg 60 mg · over 40 kg 75 mg.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Influenza' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Influenza/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Involve the paediatric team** for suspected influenza with risk factors for severe disease; **consider transfer** for severe disease or care beyond the local hospital.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Influenza' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Influenza/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge a well child** once carers have been taught to watch for complications; consider community follow-up (community nursing, hospital in the home, virtual ED or GP).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Influenza' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Influenza/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Vaccination is the best prevention:** yearly; funded and strongly recommended for children from 6 months to under 5 years, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children, children with risk factors, and pregnant women. Hand and respiratory hygiene also reduce spread.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Influenza' (Last updated January 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Influenza/, retrieved 2026-09-23
